name: New Hampshire
summary: Statutes: gc.nh.gov (General Court) serves one HTML page per RSA section plus a whole-chapter '-mrg' page. URLs are constructible once the title (Roman) is known from the title index, which shows chapter ranges. The site says it is current through the 2026 regular session and is not official. The script route fails because gc.nh.gov drops the connection, and WebFetch waits for approval on built URLs, so use URLs taken from index pages. Justia (2025) is the tier-2 fallback. Constitution: the official nh.gov page could not be read; Justia's copy is dated 1990. Court rules are on courts.nh.gov as long single pages: WebFetch reads them but cuts them off (Evidence after Rule 902, Criminal Procedure in Rule 23), and the host blocks the script with a bot check. These are corpus candidates. Admin rules: gc.nh.gov per-chapter HTML (not official), Cornell LII per section (script ok), and a weekly Rulemaking Register in PDF. Case law: neutral citations ('2024 N.H. 1', paragraph pinpoints) since 1 Jan. 2024. Slip opinions are on courts.nh.gov, but the listing could not be read (WebFetch gated, script blocked). Justia has HTML by year. Certiorari history is on supremecourt.gov dockets ('Lower Ct: Supreme Court of New Hampshire'), which the script reads.

citation_map.notes: RSA citations are distinctive ('RSA 358-A:2', chapter:section with a colon). The URL also needs the title as a Roman numeral, which a citation does not carry; take it from the chapter ranges on https://gc.nh.gov/rsa/html/nhtoc.htm. Subdivisions are Roman numerals after a comma ('RSA 126-G:2, I'), so do not read the ', I' as part of the section. Neutral citations ('2024 N.H. 1') have a four-digit year and N.H. Reports citations ('176 N.H. 319') have a three-digit volume; the regex keeps the two apart. Bare 'Sup. Ct. R. 7', 'Superior Court Rule 12', bare agency-prefixed rule numbers ('Env-Wq 1001.01', 'Ban 101.01'), bare docket numbers and 'cert. denied' are context_required. The Supreme Court's nonprecedential final orders (Sup. Ct. R. 12-D) are cited by docket number and date. CourtListener ids 'nh' and 'nhsuperct' are from memory and unverified.

sources.title: New Hampshire Revised Statutes Online (RSA)
sources.publisher: New Hampshire General Court (Office of Legislative Services)
sources.official_status_evidence: https://gc.nh.gov/rsa/html/indexes/default.aspx footer: 'THE MATERIAL AVAILABLE ON THIS WEBSITE, WHILE BELIEVED TO BE ACCURATE, IS PROVIDED FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY.' No UELMA authentication statement seen.
sources.coverage: All RSA titles I-LXV. One HTML page per section, plus a whole-chapter page {chapter}-mrg.htm.

access.pattern_rules: title_roman: the RSA title in upper-case Roman numerals. A citation does not give it: look it up in the chapter ranges on https://gc.nh.gov/rsa/html/nhtoc.htm ('TITLE XXXI: TRADE AND COMMERCE (Includes Chapters 333 - 359-V)'). chapter: as cited, with an upper-case letter suffix (567-A, 126-G). section: the part after the colon; the colon becomes a hyphen (567-A:1 → 567-A-1.htm). Whole chapter: https://gc.nh.gov/rsa/html/{title_roman}/{chapter}/{chapter}-mrg.htm. Chapter TOC: https://gc.nh.gov/rsa/html/NHTOC/NHTOC-{title_roman}-{chapter}.htm. Lettered sections (507:7-d) are not verified; the case of the suffix is unknown, so confirm through the chapter TOC. The older host www.gencourt.state.nh.us serves the same paths.
access.navigation: nhtoc.htm (titles with chapter ranges) → NHTOC/NHTOC-{title}.htm (chapters) → NHTOC/NHTOC-{title}-{chapter}.htm (section links and the -mrg whole-chapter link) → section page.
